posts.author: Jeffrey Weil
posts.content_md:
When I have a flat, I have a short table that can fit under the table and take the weight. I put a car jack on that and just lift up the flat side of the table with a bit of 2x4 between the jack and the table to protect it and disperse the load a bit. From there I can slide the bad tire out and replace it. Easy.

Since I'm using magnetic mounts and not tilting the table that far I don't need to remove any optics before jacking it up. 

Place a bit of wood in the donut hole of the new inner tube before you inflate it. That way if it goes flat the tire's not crushed and you don't have to jack that far to remove it.

posts.author: jsfisher
posts.content_md:
I'm playing with related stuff.

Holography is a hobby for me, one which I do very badly, but so what. Any good hobby should be a sink for vast sums of money, so, that's what I do. Most of the holograms I produce are crap, but occasionally I produce something that is merely garbage. Right now, I am exploring two areas.

The first involves 405nm laser diodes, but I am in need of a suitable constant current power supply.

The other is with spin coating. The goal is to use a hard drive spindle motor as the center-piece with computer control and a vacuum hold system and all that. As it turns out, hard drive spindles are extremely hard to control at low speeds, and there in lies the challenge which keeps the hobby interesting....

Oh, and I update the HoloWiki on occasion.

posts.author: John Klayer
posts.content_md:
I shot a few in a cave this past Sunday morning. There was a bit involved in it. I was up all Friday night making finishing touches on my latest cave holography contraption. I got on the road early Saturday morning and arrived in north Georgia around 11:00 AM. It was raining like crazy. I got completely drenched getting the equipment to the cave which has a small pit entrance. I lowered the equipment down on a couple of ropes then I rappelled down to move the stuff back farther into the cave. I thought I saw a snake skin but it just turned out to just be a piece of webbing that a previous caver left behind. I don’t like snakes. I left the equipment to temperature stabilize and climbed out expecting to come back in a few hours. It was still raining when I got out. I met up with a couple of my caving buddies who were also soaking wet from hiking all morning looking for new caves. We went to a small cabin that one of them owns and it eventually quit raining so we decided to go watch the 150th anniversary reenactment of the battle of Chickamauga a few miles away.

Later that evening after supper and drying my caving coveralls over the campfire, I planned to go back to the cave to shoot but I heard a pack of coyotes howling somewhere in the direction of the cave. I don’t like coyotes either. I got some sleep then went to the cave in the morning. I brought five plates of Ultimate 08. I ruined the first by accidentally leaving a black card in the reference beam during exposure. I didn’t get around to developing them till Monday morning. One turned out great and the other three just okay. I need to play around some with times and ratios.

posts.author: Jeffrey Weil
posts.content_md:
Ok, here's the first proof of my hockey card. It's a bit dinged up from shipping, that's why the color changes on the right side in a few places. The proof is quickly embossed so the client can approve the image before things move ahead into full production. 

[](https://holographyforum.org/forum/download/file.php?id=2409&mode=view)

It's a full color, 3 level, 2d-3d. The background which looks like cracked ice. A black and white Lord Stanley which looks pretty burned out. The art they gave me for him was many generations old and looked just like that. And then the rainbow colored Stanley Cup in real space. 

Lord Stanley is black and white but not a true achromat. It's a full color mix of a black and white object. A true achromatic hologram would have been made with an open aperture master. 

I've made many 2d-3d's over the last 25 years but this is the first time someone has asked for pure black to fade into transparency showing the layer behind it. The fade looks better in real life, more gradual. I like how it came out. I'll post the finished card after it's produced. The hologram will be cropped down to fit into the card properly. This image contains lots of bleed.

posts.author: John Klayer
posts.content_md:
The latest transmission holograms I shot were on 27 October in a different cave than the "Holo Hole" in north Georgia that I usually use. A couple turned out not bad. I tried a couple of reflection holograms with a hillbilly rigged fiber optic as a last minute thought - one of them was sort of okay.

This is one view my latest cave holography contraption, which I will soon modify again to make it smaller: 

![Image](http://i39.tinypic.com/2eeewzc.jpg)

This is a different view of it:

![Image](http://i43.tinypic.com/2qsnk2d.jpg)

The contraption consists of a C315 laser, shutter, 1/2 wave plate, polarizing beam splitter, LSD (light shaping diffuser), space filter, transfer mirror, convex reference expanding mirror and platten to the hold plate. I also included two fans for cooling.

Here it is in the other cave, which the land owner wants to keep secret. This isn't even the pretty part of the cave, it's just as far as I could get in my present condition. I've been to the real pretty stuff a long time ago. Maybe if I lose about 20 pounds and 15 years of age, I could go farther. I hurt for several days after.

![Image](http://i40.tinypic.com/289ddzl.jpg)

That stuff on the floor was strange, some kind of sticky sand.
